Unified sample size calculator (three-axis API)

Source: R/calculate.R
calculate.Rd

Computes sample size (or events/cases) for a study design identified by the triple design / task / outcome. See docs/DESIGN_MATRIX.md (source repository) for the complete combination table, formulas, and literature sources.

Usage

calculate(...)

Arguments

...

... Control and design arguments, resolved by EXACT name (partial matching is deliberately avoided so that design-specific arguments such as d cannot be swallowed by the design slot).

Control arguments

  • design (first positional argument): one of "rct", "paired", "rctSingleArm", "crossover", "bioequivalence", "singleArmPhaseII", "cohort", "caseControl", "caseControlMatched", "crosstab", "singleProportion", "singleMean", "singleCorrelation", "diagAccuracy", "diagAccuracyCompare", "diagAUC", "diagAUCCompare", "diagLR", "clusterRCT", "steppedWedge", "twoOrdinal", "predictiveModel", "kappa", "its" - the study-design axis.

  • task (second positional argument): "test", "estimate", "noninferiority", "superiority", "equivalence", or "plan"; optional for unambiguous designs.

  • outcome (third positional argument): "mean", "proportion", "rate", "survival", "auc", "lr", "correlation", "ordinal", or "events"; optional for unambiguous designs.

  • alpha: scalar in (0, 1), default 0.05. Use 0.025 for one-sided non-inferiority trials spending a full two-sided 0.05.

  • power: scalar in (0, 1), default 0.8 (80 percent); 0.9 for confirmatory trials.

Design-specific parameters (all validated; ranges shown):

  • RCT, test, mean: mean1, mean2 real-valued group means (e.g. mmHg); sd > 0 pooled standard deviation.

  • RCT, test, proportion: p1, p2 in (0, 1) response rates, must differ.

  • RCT, test, survival: hr in (0, 1) anticipated hazard ratio (<1 = benefit); pE in (0, 1) experimental-arm share (default 0.5). Returns events required.

  • RCT, noninferiority/superiority, mean or proportion: same inputs as above plus margin > 0 (NI margin Delta, one-sided alpha; or the minimal clinically important difference for superiority).

  • RCT, equivalence, mean or proportion: margin = corridor half-width; must exceed |mean1 - mean2| (or |p1 - p2|); uses Z_(beta/2).

  • paired, mean: meanDiff != 0 within-subject mean difference; sdDiff > 0 SD of the differences (NOT the pooled SD).

  • paired, proportion: p1, p2 in (0, 1); psi in (0, 1) expected discordant-pair proportion, psi >= |p1-p2|; output in pairs.

  • rctSingleArm, mean: mu0 historical mean, mu1 anticipated mean, sigma > 0.

  • rctSingleArm, proportion: p0 historical rate, p1 anticipated rate, both in (0, 1).

  • crossover, mean: delta > 0 treatment difference; sigma_within > 0 within-subject SD.

  • bioequivalence: cv in (0, 1) intra-subject CV; theta0 GMR inside the acceptance range (default 1.0); margin_low/margin_high default 0.8/1.25 (80-125 rule).

  • singleArmPhaseII: p0 unacceptable rate; p1 > p0 target rate; optimizer = "optimal" or "minimax".

  • cohort, proportion: p0, p1 in (0, 1); ratio >= 1 unexposed:exposed; optional dropout in [0, 1) inflates by 1/(1-d).

  • cohort, rate: rate0, rate1 > 0 events per person-time; ratio at least 1 person-time ratio.

  • caseControl: p0 in (0, 1) control exposure rate; OR > 0, != 1; m >= 1 controls per case (default 1).

  • caseControlMatched: p0, OR as above; 1:1 matching built in.

  • crosstab: p0, p1 in (0, 1) prevalence in unexposed/exposed.

  • singleProportion: p in (0, 1); precision > 0; precision_type = "absolute" (default) or "relative".

  • singleMean: sigma > 0; precision > 0 margin of error.

  • singleCorrelation: r in (0, 1); exactly one of precision (absolute CI half-width in (0, 1)) or epsilon (relative).

  • diagAccuracy, estimate: prob in (0, 1) expected Se/Sp; d in (0, 1) CI half-width; prevalence in (0, 1]; optional ci_method = "precision" (Zhou Eq 6.2) or "ci_width_power" (Eq 6.1, uses power).

  • diagAccuracy, test: prob, p0 in (0, 1); method = "asymptotic" or "exact" (A'Hern); dual-endpoint adds prob_spec, p0_spec, dual = TRUE, dual_power (default 0.90).

  • diagAccuracyCompare: p1, p2 in (0, 1); paired = TRUE requires psi in (0, 1); margin tasks add margin in (0, 1).

  • diagAUC, estimate: auc in (0, 1); d > 0; ratio >= 1 case:control (default 1); var_method = "binormal" (recommended), "exponential", or "conservative".

  • diagAUC, test: auc, auc0 in (0, 1), auc > auc0.

  • diagAUCCompare: auc1, auc2 in (0, 1); r in [0, 1) (default 0.5); margin tasks add margin in (0, 1).

  • diagLR, estimate: sens, spec in (0, 1); lr_type = "positive" or "negative"; target_lr > 0 the boundary the CI must not cross.

  • clusterRCT: base two-group args plus icc in [0, 1) and cluster_size integer >= 1 (DE = 1 + (m-1)*ICC).

  • steppedWedge: theta != 0; tau2 > 0; sigma2_ind > 0; m >= 1; n_clusters integer >= 2, a multiple of clusters_per_step >= 1.

  • twoOrdinal: or > 0, != 1; prop_bar positive vector summing to 1.

  • predictiveModel, binary: prev in (0, 1); n_parameters integer at least 1; r2_cs within its feasible maximum; shrinkage default 0.9; mape default 0.05; precision_delta default 0.05.

  • predictiveModel, rate: rate > 0 per person-year; timepoint > 0; precision_delta in (0, 1); optional n_parameters/epv cross-check.

  • predictiveModel, events: n_parameters >= 1; epv >= 1 (classic 10); event_prevalence in (0, 1).

  • kappa, estimate: pi1, pi2 in (0, 1); kappa in [0, 1); d in (0, 1).

  • kappa, test: kappa1 != kappa2 in (0, 1); same pi's.

  • its: effect_sd > 0; n_pre, n_post integers >= 3 (>= 8 recommended); rho in [0, 1). Returns achieved power.

  • caseControlMatched: p0, OR as above; 1:1 matching built in.

  • crosstab: p0, p1 in (0, 1) prevalence in unexposed/exposed.

Value

Object of class sample_size_result with print, summary, and plot methods. Default printing shows sample sizes, the plain-text formula (formula), LaTeX source (formula_latex), calculation process (calculation_steps, also available as calculation), and literature references (reference). New-style objects also carry axis metadata (task, outcome, design_canonical, results, roles, adjustments). summary.sample_size_result() additionally lists all input parameters and recorded adjustments.

Examples

# Antihypertensive RCT: placebo 10 mmHg vs new drug 12 mmHg SBP reduction,
# pooled SD 3 mmHg, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power
calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison"
#> • Sample size per group: 37
#> • Total sample size: 74
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha =
#> 0.05, power = 0.80).
#> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common
#> SD sigma = 3.
#> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha =
#> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80).
#> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 *
#> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 =
#> 35.32.
#> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration
#> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2).
#> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74.
#> Reference:
#> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# Generic vs originator antidiabetic, non-inferiority margin 1 point,
# one-sided alpha 0.05
calculate(
  design = "rct", task = "noninferiority", outcome = "mean",
  mean1 = 10, mean2 = 9.5, sd = 3, margin = 1
)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Non-inferiority (means)"
#> • Sample size per group: 50
#> • Total sample size: 100
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2+margin)^2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}\right)^2$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: State non-inferiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= -margin vs H1: mu1
#> - mu2 > -margin (margin Delta = 1, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80).
#> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 + margin = 10 - 9.50 + 1 =
#> 1.50; SD sigma = 3.
#> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta =
#> 0.8416.
#> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 /
#> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 0.8416)^2 * 3^2 / (1.50)^2 = 49.46.
#> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 50 per group, total sample size N = 100.
#> Reference:
#> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). *Sample size calculations in clinical research* (3rd ed.). CRC Press. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# Bioequivalence of a generic amlodipine: intra-subject CV 25%,
# expected GMR 1.0, 80-125% acceptance range (2x2 crossover)
calculate("bioequivalence", cv = 0.25)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Bioequivalence (2x2 crossover, exact TOST noncentral t)"
#> • Required sample size: 12
#> • Total sample size: 24
#> • Power achieved: 0.8372
#> Parameter roles
#> 
#> • cv = intra-subject coefficient of variation (log scale implied)
#> • theta0 = anticipated geometric mean ratio (true ratio, default 1.0)
#> • margin = [0.80, 1.25] average BE criteria
#> • n is per sequence; total subjects = 2n
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `exact TOST (Phillips 1990): power = pt(-t, df, ncp=d2) - pt(t, df, ncp=d1)`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$\text{Power} = F_t(-t_{1-\alpha,\, \nu};\, \nu,\, \delta_2) - F_t(t_{1-\alpha,\, \nu};\, \nu,\, \delta_1), \quad \nu = N-2$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: Intra-subject variance on log scale: sigma_w = sqrt(ln(1 + CV^2)) =
#> sqrt(ln(1 + 0.25^2)) = 0.2462.
#> • Step 2: Standard BE log-scale boundaries: [ln(0.80), ln(1.25)] = [-0.2231,
#> 0.2231].
#> • Step 3: Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) under assumed geometric mean ratio theta0
#> = 1.
#> • Step 4: Search sequence sample size n by evaluating the difference of
#> noncentral t distribution probabilities (Phillips 1990; df = 2n - 2).
#> • Step 5: Required sample size: n = 12 per sequence (achieved power = 0.8372,
#> Total N = 24).
#> Reference:
#> Primary: Phillips, K. F. (1990). Power of the two one-sided tests procedure in bioequivalence. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 18(2), 137-144.
#> 
#>  Also: Julious, S. A. (2004). Tutorial in biostatistics: sample sizes for clinical trials with normal data. Statistics in Medicine, 23, 1921-1986 (Eq 13, p. 1941);
#>  Schuirmann, D. J. (1987). J Pharmacokinet Biopharm, 15(6), 657-680;
#>  Chow & Liu (2009). Design and Analysis of Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# Colorectal cancer screening kit: expected sensitivity 85%,
# CI half-width +/-5%, clinic prevalence 20%
calculate("diagAccuracy", "estimate", "proportion",
  prob = 0.85, d = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20
)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Diagnostic accuracy (single)"
#> • Cases needed: 196
#> • Total subjects to screen: 980
#> • Total subjects: 980
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2)^2 * P*(1-P)/d^2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n_{{{cases}}} = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: Specify diagnostic accuracy prob (Se or Sp) = 0.85, margin of error d
#> = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20 (alpha = 0.05).
#> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level =
#> 95%).
#> • Step 3: Calculate target cases required: n_cases = Z_sum^2 * prob * (1 -
#> prob) / d^2 = (1.96)^2 * 0.85 * 0.15 / (0.05)^2 = 195.91.
#> • Step 4: Adjust for disease prevalence: total subjects to screen = n_cases /
#> prevalence = 195.91 / 0.20 = 979.57.
#> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target cases needed = 196, Total subjects to
#> screen = 980.
#> Reference:
#> Primary: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36.
#> 
#> Review: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# AUC precision for a biomarker validation cohort: AUC 0.80,
# CI half-width 0.10, 1:1 case:control, binormal variance
calculate("diagAUC", auc = 0.80, d = 0.05, var_method = "binormal")
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Single-group AUC CI precision"
#> • Cases needed: 184
#> • Total subjects to screen: 368
#> • Total subjects: 368
#> Parameter roles
#> 
#> • auc = anticipated area under the ROC curve
#> • precision = desired CI half-width L
#> • ratio = case:control ratio R (cases:non-cases; default 1)
#> • var_method = binormal variance function
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2 / d)^2 * V(AUC)`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n_{cases} = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2 \cdot V(AUC)$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: Anticipated AUC = 0.80, precision d = 0.05, supplied allocation R =
#> 1, alpha = 0.05.
#> • Step 2: Use the binormal variance model with the supplied allocation: V(AUC)
#> = 0.1195.
#> • Step 3: Calculate cases: n_cases = (Z_(1-alpha/2)/d)^2 * V(AUC) =
#> (1.96/0.05)^2 * 0.1195 = 183.56.
#> • Step 4: Convert using the supplied allocation: total = n_cases*(1+R) =
#> 183.56*(1+1) = 367.12.
#> • Step 5: Round up: Target cases needed = 184, Total subjects to screen = 368.
#> Reference:
#> Primary: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.). Wiley. Section 6.1.2, pp. 196-199 (Eq 6.4/6.5/6.6; CTC worked example).
#> 
#>  Original variance: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). Radiology, 143(1), 29-36.
#>  Binormal variance: Obuchowski, N. A. (1994). Medical Decision Making, 14(2), 154-162. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>
